newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares follow Wall Street down at close.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares follow Wall Street down at close.

text.p: Italian shares closed mostly lower on Tuesday hit by the stronger than expected housing data out of the United States which sent shudders through Wall Street and all major European stock exchanges.

The data sparked fears of higher interest rates -- traditionally a signal for stock investors to sell. The all share Mibtel index finished 0.22 percent lower at 10.293 while the Mib30 blue chip index ended 0.16 percent down at 15,373.
Telecom stocks, which rose on Monday after the Treasury announced details of the purchase of state holding group IRI's dominant stake in telecoms group Stet, also eased back on profit-taking.

"Treasury bonds and the street came off on the U.S. housing data and we followed it on the way down," said a Milan stocks trader. "Milan had been pretty directionless until then and was waiting for a lead."
Energy group ENI eased 0.32 percent to 7,787 lire, but was well supported after CSFB declared it was its international focus stock of the week.
Market watchers said they expected a fairly subdued run until the end of the year after many international funds appeared to have closed their books ahead of the Christmas festivities.
Interpump shares dropped 6.65 percent to 5,023 lire, the second day of losses after the company's debut on the exchange.

Fiat was also marked down, finishing 1.42 percent lower at 4,302 lire while Olivetti reacted positively to news that Bell Atlantic is to buy 5.8 percent of mobile phone operator Omnitel from Olivetti.
